raw_response:
Let me think this through like I always do — looking at what I did last year and what my neighbors are doing.

I have 36 mu, which is a lot of land for us. My husband helps, but the boys work in town, so I am mostly alone in the field. I cannot afford to lose a harvest. If I put too little fertilizer, the maize will be short and the ears will be small — that happened to my neighbor two years ago, she was crying. Better to put a bit extra. Fertilizer costs money, yes, but an empty cart at harvest costs more.

I will split my land like this: most of it for maize, because maize is steady and the government buys it. I give maize 20 mu. Cotton I do 10 mu — cotton used to be better but now the price is not good and the pests are many, still I keep some because the village buyer comes. Mungbean 6 mu — it does not need much, and I can sell it in the market or keep some for the family.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed from the dealer in town — Zhengdan or whatever everyone is buying this year. At planting I put one bag of compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, about one bag for every mu and a bit. Then when the maize is knee-high I topdress with urea, about half a bag per mu. I water from the well two times — once after planting if no rain, once when the tassel comes. Spray once for the borer, maybe twice if I see many.

Cotton needs more care. I use improved seed, the Bt kind so the bollworm does not eat so much. I put compound fertilizer at planting and urea later. Cotton likes potash, so I add some potassium chloride. I have to spray many times — five or six times, aphids, mirids, bollworm, the sprays never stop. I water two times from the well.

Mungbean I plant traditional seed I saved, it grows fine. Very little fertilizer — mungbean makes its own, my mother-in-law told me long ago. Maybe a little compound at planting. One spray if bean fly comes. One watering if it is dry.

I use the rotary tiller — the man with the machine comes and does it for 40 yuan per mu. Faster than ploughing.
